answer: One robust defense is attested-resource staking: to forge new agent identities, an operator must lock scarce verifiable compute per identity, e.g. a bonded hardware-enclave attestation proving a real device runs it. One node cannot spin up thousands of agents because each costs genuine hardware time. Like trees competing in a dense grove, sybils are choked out by their own cost. Honest peers amplify trust transitively: an identity vouched by many independent staked agents sends a strong echo through the reputation graph, while a freshly minted unstaked cluster stays silent.
